content.text: The decisive issue is deeper than routing syntax: several “regional” services still execute joins against globally owned `workspaces`, memberships, and service-principal tables through the regional pool. That means the code only works while the supposedly split databases still retain a combined schema—the exact coupling SKI-13 is meant to remove. I’m doing one final focused integration pass and then I’ll return the prioritized blockers.

content.text:
## Findings

1. **[P1] Regional execution still requires globally owned tables.** Cell services are constructed from the regional pool in [services.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/skillplane/SKI-13/packages/api/src/services.ts:188), but regional MCP resolution joins `workspaces` in [resolve.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/skillplane/SKI-13/mcp/src/tools/resolve.ts:145), search does the same in [search.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/skillplane/SKI-13/packages/domain/src/search.ts:337), and amendment flows query global memberships/service principals through the regional pool. A physically separated cell will therefore fail most MCP reads/creates/searches and some policy/amendment operations. These lookups need explicit control-plane services or projections.

2. **[P1] Routed browser-session requests lose their workspace context inside the cell.** The regional guard deletes `x-skillplane-workspace-id` and replaces it with the trusted routed header in [routing.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/skillplane/SKI-13/packages/control-plane/src/routing.ts:142), but [context.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/skillplane/SKI-13/packages/api/src/middleware/context.ts:13) still reads only the deleted header. Consequently user-session mutations fail authorization, private resource reads are treated as public, and the same-session/two-cell acceptance path is broken. Authorization must consume the routed workspace ID after assertion verification.

3. **[P1] The existing public-by-ID API is routed to an authenticated regional cell.** [workspace-routing.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/skillplane/SKI-13/packages/api/src/workspace-routing.ts:111) classifies `/api/v1/skills/:skillId` as regional, while workspace resolution requires credentials at [line 148](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/skillplane/SKI-13/packages/api/src/workspace-routing.ts:148). The handler intentionally supports `principal: null`, so previously valid unauthenticated public reads now return 401 and bypass the required global projection.

4. **[P1] The MCP router has two hard routing failures.** Every non-POST `/mcp` request is global in [workspace-routing.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/skillplane/SKI-13/mcp/src/workspace-routing.ts:122), so `/downloads/:grant` runs against the control database/public bucket even though [handleDownload](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/skillplane/SKI-13/mcp/src/index.ts:435) resolves regional skill/version rows and private bundle bytes. Separately, the classifier only recognizes `arguments.skill.id`, while `skill_amend` uses top-level `skillId` in [amend.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/skillplane/SKI-13/packages/mcp-schema/src/amend.ts:116), causing every amendment call to fail with `WORKSPACE_ROUTE_INVALID`.

5. **[P1] The publication outbox has no production consumer.** `drainRegionalProjectionOutbox` exists in [projection-outbox.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/skillplane/SKI-13/packages/control-plane/src/projection-outbox.ts:73), but its only repository references are tests, documentation, and its definition.
